Also, from the document attached to this Official Note, the excerpt from the register of death and the certificate of death, we only see that death occurred and in which way it occurred. We do not see that it was caused by a sniper, that it was due to sniper activity or shelling or any projectile coming from the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are doing is to explain that the probative value is not covering all elements. This doesn't deprive it from its probative value, but we'll decide once we've seen the translation of the attachment, we'll decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just, for the record, mention that earlier we had ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Earlier the number P7527 had been provisionally assigned to 32942 that's when we asked for this underlying documents. Now if we give 7527 to 32942a and the 7527 at 32942 must be vacated. And then 32942 has, then, not been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. As long as that is understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I earlier said that I wanted to MFI the document but gave an opportunity to Mr. Lukic to -- to express whether he would still stand by his objections, I didn't MFI but I hereby MFI the document, awaiting the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I could deal with the exhibits after the break, Your Honour. It would be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's better to do that. Mr. Lukic, as far as timing is concerned, any changes in your assessment you gave yesterday? MR. S. LUKIC: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any changes? MR. S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] No, no changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll first take a break. We'll -- after the break, first deal with some other documents, and you'll then have an opportunity to cross-examine [sic] the witness, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Tusevljak, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, if you would already start when waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Absolutely. The exhumation report that we discussed with respect to Mr. Zlatko Knezevic, that was 65 ter number 12222, I would ask be admitted as a Prosecution Exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 12222 receives exhibit number P7529 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And 65 ter 11229, the death certificate for Jadranka Tenzera, if that could be the final last Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 11229 becomes Exhibit P7530, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I had understood that this was already part of P867.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We've been looking into that, and we'll be able to sort it out outside the courtroom. We're unable to verify at this moment whether or not it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready to re-examine the witness, you may proceed. MR. S. LUKIC: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Tusevljak.

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you yesterday about persons who disappeared in the area of the municipality of Olovo. That's page T38488, lines 16 through 18. I should like to call up D1216. MR. S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] I would only like to ask for assistance because I don't have the page at this moment. I only have the number of the person I'm looking for. It's under number 299. I don't know if that's enough. I apologise, just a moment. Yes, thank you. Could we just move the page a little, both in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But yesterday at that page you indicated Ms. Edgerton talked about number 229.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: MR. S. LUKIC: My mistake. I should say 229. That's the page 21 on B/C/S. Same page on English -- in English. [Interpretation] Could we again move the document to the left, both versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, it was shown to you that this person disappeared in Olovo in December 1993. In the course of your investigations, what did you establish, where were Sarajevo Serbs taken? What are all the places to which they were taken?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Sarajevo Serbs who went missing in Sarajevo now we see that their bodies are being exhumed in Zenica and in other areas outside Sarajevo. They're being found elsewhere. The persons who went missing in Sarajevo, their bodies were transported after the war. There have been many sanitisations of the terrain drives and their bodies were scattered everyone where. We addressed to the office for missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina and other services in charge of sanitisation and the city funeral homes of Sarajevo but we never got many answers. Also, the prosecutor who was working together with us and who was giving us orders tried to get this information but the answer we most frequently got was that documentation had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any specific knowledge about this entry? I mean, you're telling us in general terms what happened to people, taken where, transported after the war. Do you have any specific knowledge about this 229 entry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I told you, I really have no specific knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. MR. S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Could we now look at page 61 of this same document, both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: We should focus on number 707 here. Denda, Tihomir Denda, son of Krsto. Looking at these notes, can you tell us what Unis, Unis, is?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unis was a large company in Sarajevo that had its shops and warehouses in different area, including one warehouse in the territory of Hrasna. This is a reference to the Unis warehouse that was one of the camps and one of the detention facilities holding Serbs during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask Ms. Edgerton, if you yesterday referred to 707 or 706? The transcript of yesterday indicates 707 but you referred specifically to Olovo yesterday and I see in 706 the person went missing on the 16th of January, 1994 in Olovo. Was that what you wanted to refer to.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, only Olovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But then yesterday the number was wrongly recorded at least. It's not 707 but 706; right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It could well have been my mistake in the numbers, but, yes, Your Honour, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to alert you, Mr. Lukic, what the topic was about yesterday about that part of the cross-examination, it was related to Olovo. MR. S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that the reference was to Olovo, but completely different numbers and different names were put on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: You were also asked yesterday by my learned friend where the village of Kijevo is located. Can you tell us whose municipality is that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the municipality of Trnovo, and it's one of ten Sarajevo municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. S
utterances.text: Could we now look at document 33024? That's the 65 ter number. MR. S. LUKIC: I think there is only English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. S

utterances.text: That we can continue. Then I'd like to first deliver an oral decision on the Prosecution's request to replace P3207. P3207 being a redacted statement of Witness Predrag Radulovic's with -- to be replaced with document bearing Rule 65 ter number 30594A, an unredacted version. This decision is related to prior decisions, which the Chamber will recall first. On the 4th of October, 2013, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking to admit Radulovic's statement and 29 associated exhibits pursuant to Rule 92 quater. The Defence opposed this motion. On 20th December 2013, the Chamber admitted the statement with the exclusion of paragraph 133 and denied admission of the associated exhibit bearing Rule 65 ter number 26215. On the 26 February 2014 the Chamber upheld its decision following a Prosecution motion to reconsider. Paragraph 133 of Radulovic's statement quotes documents -- the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 26215, which states that at a meeting Mladic and Colonel Slavko Lisica "pointed out that ethnic cleansing should be carried out in Teslic municipality as soon as and as efficiently as possible," and that "Mladic allegedly advised some members of the Serbian army and the SDS to set on fire and kill Muslims and Croats wherever they could, that they would not be held responsible in any way and that he could issue them with a written guarantee for that." The Chamber, at that time, concluded that the admission of paragraph 133 of the statement, as well as document bearing Rule 65 ter number 26215 without the benefit of cross-examination would be unduly prejudicial to the accused and therefore merited exclusion under Rule 89(D). On the 30th of September, 2014, the Defence filed a motion to present Nedjo Vlaski's evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter and included document bearing Rule 65 ter number 26215 as an associated exhibit on its exhibit list. In his statement and during his testimony Vlaski commented on this document. The Prosecution then tendered the document and it was admitted into evidence as Exhibit P6890. The Prosecution then sought to replace the redacted statement of Radulovic with an unredacted version currently bearing Rule 65 ter number 30594A. The sole difference between the two versions is the exclusion of paragraph 133 in the redacted version. On 4 November 2014 the Chamber directed the Defence in court to respond to this request at a later time. On the 15th of December, 2014, and the 2nd of March, 2015, the Chamber, via e-mail, again asked the Defence to respond. As of today's date, the Defence has not responded and the Chamber will now decide on the Prosecution's request. When the Chamber delivered its original decision excludeing paragraph 133 of Radulovic's statement document bearing Rule 65 ter number 26215 was not in evidence. Now, this document including the alleged statements of the accused during the meeting, the citing of which formed the basis for the initial exclusion of paragraph 133, has been admitted into evidence, as P6890. Radulovic did not participate in this meeting and only commented on the document. As such, paragraph 133 does not add significantly to the document's probative value. Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the admission of paragraph 133 into evidence without the benefit of cross-examination of Radulovic is no longer unduly prejudicial to the accused. The Chamber therefore grants the Prosecution request and instructs the Registry to replace P3207 with document bearing 65 ter number 30594A. As a final matter, the Chamber recalls that the weight to be attributed to paragraph 133 of Radulovic's statement will be assessed in the context of all the evidence before the Chamber, and that this decision deals only with the admission of this paragraph. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.text: We are not, at this moment -- you have not responded to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Still, the rules are the rules. Acts and conduct of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it would have been preferable you would have brought that to our attention. At this moment the ruling is there and whatever the consequences are for the future, you can try to make up your mind yourself. But Judge Moloto would like to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This paragraph was excluded because it was being tendered as a 92 quater statement and without cross-examination that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then you, the Defence, tendered the same paragraph. Now when you tender it yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not the paragraph, the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document which contains the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Remind me, Mr. Lukic, by telling me where exactly in Rule 92 quater where the acts and conduct of the accused is excluded as a subject matter in a statement. Could you read -- I mean, I rather that's in 92 bis. It doesn't apply in 92 ter but could you remind me because you relied on 92 quater where that is to be found as exclusive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 92 quater is also without cross-examination [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I'm asking you where in the rule because I think Rule 92 quater is pretty precise on that. But I am asking my colleagues to -- let me see. I don't have my glasses with me, but. "If the evidence goes to proof of acts and conduct of an accused as charged in the indictment, that may be a factor against the admission of such evidence or that part of it." Which means that Rule 92 quater explicitly allows, though with caution, admission of a statement going to the acts and conduct of the accused and that therefore if you compare it to 92 bis you're missing part of what Rule 92 quater says. So although it would have been if you first consulted Rule 92 quater before asking the question, I hope that the Chamber has assisted you in this matter. Because you insisted on the rules to apply and that's exactly the reason why I took you to that rule. Now everyone is interfering in my programme, which I thought would take 12 to 13 minutes. I'll -- Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak at audible volume. I now deliver the Chamber's decision on the Defence motion to admit the evidence of Elliott Moore pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. On the 20th of July 2015, the Defence filed a motion pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Rules seeking admission into evidence of the undated and marked witness statement of Elliott Moore. The Defence submitted, inter alia, that although the statement is already in evidence as Exhibit D371 in the present case, the entirety of the statement should be admitted for the truth of the matters asserted therein. On the 3rd of August, the Prosecution responded to the Defence`s motion not opposing the provisional admission of the statement pending the attachment of a declaration from Moore in compliance with Rule 92 bis (B) of the Rules. Moreover, the Prosecution requested that should the marked version of the statement be admitted, Moore's declaration should also encompass the markings on the statement. The version of the statement attached to the Defence's Rule 92 bis motion differs from the version admitted as D371 insofar as a number of boxes surround portions of the statement and as it contains one illegible handwritten note. However, the Chamber notes that the content of both versions is identical. Under these circumstances, the Chamber is of the view that the markings and the note do not affect the substance of the statement to an extent that they would create a different statement. The Chamber recalls that the statement was admitted through witness John Clark on the 23rd of September, 2013, as Exhibit D371, pursuant to Rule 89(C) of the Rules. And this can be found at transcript page 17245. The Chamber further recalls that no limitations were requested or set regarding the document and therefore finds that the statement was already admitted for the truth of its content. And based on the forgoing, the Chamber declares the Defence`s motion moot. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the matter. Although I would have a few small items, I think it would be wiser, since we have spent now all the 12 or 13 minutes I assessed we would need and leave that perhaps for tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. Mr. Lukic. MR. S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] I do apologise for taking up your precious time this way, but 65 ter number 32993 is now D1217, and I wanted to tender the fourth page of that document in the B/C/S version. Since there is no translation for this fourth page, it should be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we overlooked that earlier because it's D1217 and I think it was -- we decided to admit. Whereas, since there is no full translation it should have been MFI'd. Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. If you would use our precious time - and your precious time - always so constructive, that would certainly be appreciated. We -- I leave the few other items for the days to come, and we'll adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 2nd of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
